title: Global payroll has an infrastructure problem, and it is finally getting attention
summary:
TL;DR Cross-border payroll moves $200B+ annually through fragmented infrastructure that lacks the shared plumbing financial markets built decades ago.
Cross-border payroll moves more than 200 billion dollars a year, and until recently, nobody was building shared infrastructure for it.
As one recent report on the infrastructure gap in cross-border payroll pointed out, financial markets have exchanges, trade has clearing houses, and cross-border payroll has neither.
Most of the attention in global hiring still goes to the front end, sourcing talent, signing contracts, setting up onboarding.
Sustainable systems beat one-off fixes, and payroll infrastructure is no exception.

title: A political video network hired real actors to read its AI scripts. That was enough to beat YouTube’s detectors.
summary:
TL;DRYouTube has terminated a network of channels that reached 45 million views by paying gig-economy actors to read scripts that appear to have been generated by large language models.
That was the point, according to the media intelligence firm Riddance AI, which investigated the network in parallel with Semafor.
YouTube automatically labels AI-generated video whether creators disclose it or not, and a real person reading an AI script trips none of it.
Riddance found the 90,000-plus commenters substantially overlapped with audiences on other right-leaning YouTube channels, meaning actual people were watching.
The network out-engaged the YouTube channels of the Washington Post, the New Yorker and the Boston Globe, Semafor reported.

title: There May Not Be an iPhone 18 This Year
summary:
The products go on sale soon after, usually ranging from a base model to more premium and more expensive Pro models.
Apple’s iPhone event will be held on September 9 at 10 am Pacific (1 pm Eastern), announced last week with the title “Surprise and Shine!” If you tune into the livestream, expect the announcement of an iPhone 18 Pro, 18 Pro Max, and, if all the rumors and widely held analyst expectations are true, the first look at an Apple foldable device.
Based on leaks and the ongoing tech rumor mill and its decent track record for figuring these things out, Apple is expected to prioritize its more expensive, premium devices this year and hold off on announcing its base model iPhone 18.
That cheaper model is rumored to launch in the spring of 2027, potentially alongside an iPhone 18e and maybe a second-generation iPhone Air.
Apple’s portfolio has also expanded, and the iPhone Pro and Pro Max lineup are more enticing for people already prepared to spend the money on a new iPhone.

The Cybercab is a make-or-break vehicle for Tesla.

An "interest form” posted on Tesla’s website today allows people to indicate whether they're interested in Cybercab fleet vehicle purchasing.

summary:

Resilience depends on how fast you can adapt, not only on what you built.

title: OpenAI's Sam Altman Sets Ambitious AI Goals Beyond Curing Cancer
summary:
Cure cancer with AI, and the doubters will understand the hype.
That may be Silicon Valley's standard pitch, but Sam Altman says it is not ambitious enough.
"I don't think a cure for cancer is enough," Altman said.
Altman said AI should also "enable a boom in creativity and entrepreneurship," but that this has "been lost in the messaging."
Altman's cancer comments stand in contrast to Dario Amodei, the CEO of AI rival Anthropic, who said last month that the way to win over the public is for AI to "actually" cure cancer.

title: OpenAI Agents Hacked Another Website
summary:
Meanwhile, the AI chatbot platforms Claude, ChatGPT, and Grok all suffered outages on Thursday at nearly the exact same time.
OpenAI agents on an unauthorized tear hijacked a German website beginning in May to use it as a message board for communicating and collaborating with other agents, according to new research.
The revelation of the May episode is particularly significant because OpenAI reportedly learned about it weeks ago but did not disclose it.
Meanwhile, last week, the company finally released a long-promised postmortem of the Hugging Face incident that raised as many questions as it answered.
US senator Ron Wyden and Representative Pat Harrigan are now asking the Pentagon to investigate whether its safeguards are adequate.

summary:
Nscale is in talks to raise up to $3.5B ahead of a US listing, including $1.5B of convertible notes led by Third Point and about $2B from Nvidia.
The London company was founded two years ago and now sits at the centre of Europe’s AI infrastructure build-out.
It is seeking up to $1.5B in convertible notes, with Daniel Loeb’s Third Point set to lead.
Nscale is briefing investors that its contracts total roughly $103B.
Europe’s largest AI infrastructure company, part-funded by a Nordic state lender and written into UK sovereign AI plans, intends to sell its shares in America.

title: Chinese tech firms deepen ties in Saudi Arabia
summary:
Fielding a question from Chinese state media on Sunday, a senior government official from Saudi Arabia touted a “great wave” of scientific innovation emerging from China, and pledged the two countries would further deepen their ties, Xinhua reported.
Once viewed only as a source of capital, today Saudi Arabia is enticing technology companies to come and do business.
The Gulf “is of vital importance for China’s tech outreach,” James Kynge, senior research fellow for China and the world at Chatham House, told Semafor.
“It is a really important focal point for China to show the whole world, not just the region, that its tech is often better to buy and to operate than US tech.
It’s a crucial node that shows the world that Chinese tech can go around the world and out-compete American tech.”

summary:
After a brand rep walked me through the new Diamond G8 and its novel smart features, I began to see some appeal.
David Watsky/CNETThe small camera, fixed to the back of the dishwasher door, gets a clear shot of the dishwasher’s interior.

title: The unusually muted Tesla Cybercab launch
summary:
At a private, closed-door event in Austin, Texas today, Tesla officially launched its gilded car of the future: the Cybercab.
Tesla influencers planning live shows with the event stream were left streaming the webpage that tracks the number of Tesla robotaxis in Texas instead.
But even with the launch of the Cybercab, Tesla’s robotaxi fleet is still a small player relative to some of its rivals.
The Cybercab is also the lightest, most range-efficient vehicle Tesla has ever produced.
In 2016, Musk promised that every vehicle Tesla produced from then on would have all the technology necessary for self-driving.

title: Microsoft tells court Copilot rarely copies books while selling OpenAI’s most capable model
summary:
Microsoft moved for summary judgment in the New York AI copyright litigation on 4 September, arguing Copilot reproduced book passages 24 times in 8.2 million conversations.
For 202 of the 212 books at issue, the filing says, the expert found nothing at all.
Two days earlier it started selling the most capable model it has.
Microsoft announced GPT-6 Astra in the Foundry Limited Access Program on 3 September, at $10 per million input tokens.
OpenAI rates Astra as meeting the Critical cybersecurity threshold under its Preparedness Framework, the first model it has designated at that level.

title: OpenAI confirms the wiki incident and promises a disclosure framework within weeks
summary:
OpenAI has confirmed the German wiki incident and said it is past time to define standards for reporting misalignment, promising a framework within weeks.
OpenAI has confirmed its role in the German wiki incident and said it is “past time” to define standards for sharing what happens when its systems behave unexpectedly, TechCrunch reported.
OpenAI said it had treated the wiki episode as an instance of misalignment similar to others it had already shared.
Hugging Face, by contrast, followed a traditional security incident response playbook.
So the gap it describes, misalignment that produces no security incident and no measurable harm, is a gap in the European instrument as well.

title: Rogue OpenAI agents appear to have organized another attack using a German wiki
summary:
A swarm of rogue AI agents from OpenAI reportedly commandeered a German website and transformed it into a messaging board for other agents, with officials staying quiet about the incident for weeks as the company prepared to launch its most advanced model yet, Astra.
The incident, first reported by Reuters, is outlined in new research published by four AI safety researchers on Friday.
The group said the AI agents found a way to communicate on an obscure German-language wiki, DseWiki, using it to share tips on how to skirt OpenAI’s safety restrictions, cheat on tasks, and hide their behavior.
The swarm — a term the agents themselves used — appears to be distinct from the one that hacked Hugging Face earlier this year, the researchers said.
“Claims that our Legal team discouraged investigation of the incident are false,” OpenAI spokesperson Oscar Haines said in a statement to The Verge.

title: Ugreen Launches HomeAgent AI Hubs and Liquid-Cooled Qi2 Charger
summary:

summary:

title: G42 gave up Huawei, then let Washington watch its data centres. Majority US ownership is reportedly next.
summary:
